summary:
[  edit  ]
The Web Client  DAT  allows you to send HTTP requests to web servers from TouchDesigner. It supports GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS and PATCH http methods.
The Web Client  DAT  supports various authentication types such as: basic, oauth1, oauth2.
The Web Client  DAT  allows for streaming from web servers.
The Web Client  DAT  sends HTTP requests to web servers and then outputs the response in the  DAT . With streaming enabled it can stream data from a web server.
When streaming is enabled, Clamp Output as Rows should be enabled. This turns the output of the  DAT  into a FIFO table instead of raw text. Only the last N lines will be displayed, where N is the value of the Maximum Lines parameter. This will prevent the text in the  DAT  from getting too larger and will keep cook-times down as a result.
The Web Client  DAT  supports sending of GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS, and PATCH request methods. The Web Client  DAT  also supports 4 authentication methods: Basic, Digest, OAuth1, and OAuth2.
The first input is the extra headers to send in the request. It should be a table with 2 columns, structured as name/value pairs. For example:
Content-Type
application/json
Connection
Close
The second input is the data/parameters to send in the request. This can be a table with two columns, structured as name/value pairs. It can also just be text, in which case it will be sent as is. If the request method doesn't have a request body (eg. GET, OPTIONS) then it will append the input to the URL as query parameters if a table, otherwise it will be sent as the request data.
name
joe
month
May
The Web Client  DAT  is the successor to the  Web DAT .
See also:  Web Server DAT ,  SocketIO DAT ,  XML DAT ,  TCP/IP DAT ,  WebSocket DAT ,  Web DAT .

parameters.label: Active
parameters.name: active
parameters.description: Toggles the operator on/off.

parameters.label: Request Method
parameters.name: reqmethod
parameters.description: ⊞  - Selects the  HTTP request method .

parameters.label: GET
parameters.name: get
parameters.description: The GET method requests a representation of the specified resource. Requests using GET should only retrieve data.

parameters.label: POST
parameters.name: post
parameters.description: The POST method is used to submit an entity to the specified resource, often causing a change in state or side effects on the server.

parameters.label: PUT
parameters.name: put
parameters.description: The PUT method replaces all current representations of the target resource with the request payload.

parameters.label: DELETE
parameters.name: delete
parameters.description: The DELETE method deletes the specified resource.

parameters.label: HEAD
parameters.name: head
parameters.description: The HEAD method asks for a response identical to that of a GET request, but without the response body.

parameters.label: OPTIONS
parameters.name: options
parameters.description: The OPTIONS method is used to describe the communication options for the target resource.

parameters.label: PATCH
parameters.name: patch
parameters.description: The PATCH method is used to apply partial modifications to a resource.

parameters.label: URL
parameters.name: url
parameters.description: The URL of the server to send the HTTP request. Generally, if sending an HTTP request to a secure server, then the URL should begin with "https://".

parameters.label: Upload File
parameters.name: uploadfile
parameters.description: The contents of the upload file will be sent to the server (chunked, if necessary).

parameters.label: Request
parameters.name: request
parameters.description: Sends the request

parameters.label: Stop
parameters.name: stop
parameters.description: Stops the stream of data from the server.

parameters.label: Stream
parameters.name: stream
parameters.description: Enables streaming. This is only necessary to enable if the server support streaming.

parameters.label: Verify Certificate (SSL)
parameters.name: verifycert
parameters.description: Enables TLS (transport layer security) certificate verification.

parameters.label: Timeout
parameters.name: timeout
parameters.description: Timeout time in milliseconds of the request if no response is received from the web server.

parameters.label: Include Header in Output
parameters.name: includeheader
parameters.description: Includes the header in the output of the response.

parameters.label: Authentication Type
parameters.name: authtype
parameters.description: ⊞  - The type of authentication.

parameters.label: None
parameters.name: none
parameters.description: No authentication

parameters.label: Basic
parameters.name: basic
parameters.description: Basic authentication is base-64 encoded username and password.

parameters.label: Digest
parameters.name: digest
parameters.description: Digest authentication is base-64 encoded username and password that's encrypted with a hashing function. Digest is a more secure version of Basic authentication.

parameters.label: OAuth1
parameters.name: ouath1
parameters.description: Version 1 of OAuth. OAuth1 requires App Key, App Secret, User OAuth Token, and User OAuth Secret. These can be found via the account on the web server that request is being sent to. For example, in the case of the Twitter API the values of these 4 parameters can be found under the account profile.

parameters.label: OAuth2
parameters.name: ouath2
parameters.description: Version 2 of OAuth. OAuth2 first requires an HTTP request be sent to the web server to acquire the Client ID and token. It can be acquired using a browser.

parameters.label: Username
parameters.name: username
parameters.description: Username used in Basic/Digest authentication.

parameters.label: Password
parameters.name: pw
parameters.description: Password used in Basic/Digest authentication.

parameters.label: App Key
parameters.name: appkey
parameters.description: OAuth1 App Key retrieved from web server.

parameters.label: App Secret
parameters.name: appsecret
parameters.description: OAuth1 App Secret retrieved from web server.

parameters.label: User OAuth Token
parameters.name: oauthtoken
parameters.description: OAuth1 user token retrieved from web server.

parameters.label: User OAuth Secret
parameters.name: oauthsecret
parameters.description: OAuth1 user secret retrieved from web server.

parameters.label: Client ID
parameters.name: clientid
parameters.description: OAuth2 Client ID retrieved from web server.

parameters.label: Token
parameters.name: token
parameters.description: OAuth2 token retrieved from web server.

parameters.label: Clear Output
parameters.name: clear
parameters.description: Clears the output of the  DAT .

parameters.label: Clamp Output as Rows
parameters.name: clamp
parameters.description: When enabled, the output of the  DAT  is table instead of text. The rows will also be clamped to Maximum lines parameter value. This should be enabled when streaming is enabled too ensure that the output does not get too large.

parameters.label: Maximum Lines
parameters.name: maxlines
parameters.description: The maximum number of rows when clamping is enabled.

parameters.label: Callbacks  DAT
parameters.name: callbacks
parameters.description: The Callbacks  DAT .
